sections.label: Charity governance and regulatory powers
sections.summary: The Bill aims to strengthen charity governance, accountability and transparency, and to enhance the Commissioner's regulatory powers to maintain public trust.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: First, to strengthen the governance, accountability and transparency of charities and fundraisers in Singapore, and second, to enhance the regulatory powers which the Commissioner can invoke so as to maintain a high level of public trust and confidence in the charity sector.

sections.label: Disqualification grounds and scope
sections.summary: The Bill proposes disqualifying anyone removed by the Commissioner regardless of position, and those convicted of terrorism, terrorism financing or money laundering offences.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: However, only those removed in certain specified capacities, namely trustees, governing board members or key officers, will consequentially be disqualified from assuming key positions in charities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: We propose to disqualify any person who has been removed by the Commissioner pursuant to an inquiry, regardless of his position held in a charity.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: The second proposed new ground for disqualification expressly provides that a person convicted of an offence involving terrorism, terrorism financing or money laundering will be disqualified.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: In addition to the current capacities that are proscribed, the new provision will disallow a disqualified person from indirectly managing the affairs of a charity by holding a key position in another entity which is a member or governing board member of the charity.

sections.label: Effect of removal order
sections.summary: The order will have the same effect as if the person had not resigned and was removed by the Commissioner.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: The order will have the same effect as if the person had not resigned and was removed by the Commissioner.

sections.label: Cessation of disqualification
sections.summary: The Bill clarifies a person ceases to be disqualified once his conviction is spent under the Registration of Criminals Act or he is pardoned.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: The Bill proposes to clarify that a person ceases to be disqualified once his conviction for a relevant offence is spent under the Registration of Criminals Act or if he is granted a pardon for the offence.

sections.label: Permanence of removals
sections.summary: Removals, unlike disqualifications, are permanent.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: On the other hand, removals, unlike disqualifications, are permanent.

sections.label: Definition of fundraising appeal
sections.summary: The Bill amends the definition of fundraising appeal to clarify that all fundraising appeals, big or small, online or offline, are regulated.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: The Bill thus proposes to amend the definition of "fundraising appeal" in the Act to clarify and reflect the current policy position that all fundraising appeals, whether big or small, online or offline, are subject to regulation.

sections.label: Notice before mandatory electronic filing
sections.summary: Charities will receive at least two years' notice before mandatory electronic filing begins.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: Charities will have at least two years' notice before the mandatory electronic filing takes place.

sections.label: Extending suspension of charities
sections.summary: The Bill lets the Commissioner, with the Attorney-General's consent, extend a suspension beyond 12 months up to 24 months to protect charities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: The Bill therefore seeks to protect the charities by allowing the Commissioner, with the consent of the Attorney-General, to extend the suspension beyond 12 months, up to 24 months.

sections.label: Suspension of fundraising appeals
sections.summary: Proposed amendments to section 39B let the Commissioner suspend a fundraising appeal for up to two years pending an investigation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: The proposed amendments to section 39B will allow the Commissioner to order the suspension of a fundraising appeal for a period not exceeding two years, pending the completion of an investigation.

sections.label: Commissioner's power to call documents
sections.summary: The Bill amends section 41A so the Commissioner can require documents and information a person obtains within two years after the order.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: Lastly, in relation to the Commissioner's powers to call for documents and information, the Bill proposes to amend section 41A of the Act to clarify that the Commissioner can require a person to provide information and documents that are not only already in the possession or under the control of the person, but which come into the possession or under the control of the person at a future point in time, within a period not exceeding two years after the order is made.

sections.label: Checks, governance and support for Bill
sections.summary: The passage states checks and balances exist, describes partnership and governance goals, and expresses support for the Bill's broader Commissioner powers and penalties.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: Checks and balances are also in place to ensure that these regulatory powers are exercised fairly.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: As we enhance our legislation, we will continue to build capacity to strengthen governance across the sector.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: This will be through the continued partnership between the Government, charities, stakeholders and the community.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: Together, we will achieve our vision of a well-governed and thriving charity sector with strong public support.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It entails a robust set of procedures to ensure compliance, a discipline within the organisation to comply with the procedures, a conviction ingrained in management, staff and board that we are accountable to our funders, our sponsors, our employees and, above all, our clients and their families.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Therefore, I support the Bill, particularly in the broadening of the powers of the Commissioner to protect charities and the enhancement of penalties for certain types of non-compliance.

sections.label: Questions on section 25 amendments
sections.summary: The speaker supports amendments to section 25 but asks whether suspension could extend beyond 24 months and whether subsection 12's scope could broaden.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In principle, I also support the proposed amendments to section 25.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: However, would the Minister consider making provisions for the extension of the suspension period between 24 months in complex cases, whether exercisable at the discretion of the Commissioner or upon application to court by the Commissioner?

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: A second clarification sought in relation to section 25 is: whether the Government had considered broadening the scope of section 25 subsection 12 beyond subsection (2)(iv), (v) and (vi), to include compliance with other orders of the Commissioner?

sections.label: Proxy ban for orders
sections.summary: The Minister is asked whether express provision could prohibit acting by proxy and make it an offence.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In relation to suspension, removal or disqualification orders, would the Minister consider making express provision prohibiting acting by proxy and making it an offence for persons to act by proxies?

sections.label: Registered charities and IPCs
sections.summary: The 2016 report recorded 2,247 registered charities, 653 of them IPCs, and 46.2% had receipts under $250,000 in 2015.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: According to the 2016 Annual Report of the Commissioner of Charities, there were 2,247 registered charities in 2016, of which only 653 are IPCs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In 2015, 46.2% of the registered charities had annual receipts of less than $250,000.

sections.label: Charities rely on funding
sections.summary: The current charities model relies heavily on Government funding and donations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The current charities model relies heavily on Government funding and donations.

sections.label: Time to change model
sections.summary: The speaker submits it is time to change the charities model.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Here, I submit it is time to change the charities model.

sections.label: Rethink not-for-profit rule
sections.summary: The speaker calls for rethinking and re-examining the requirement for charities to be not-for-profit.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: A model that requires us to rethink and re-examine the requirement for charities to be not-for-profit.

sections.label: Voluntary label and professionalism
sections.summary: The term voluntary masks the need for professionalism, and sentiment grows to drop the VWO label, a 2016 NCSS conversation that should continue.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The term "voluntary" masks the need for professionalism in service delivery and in the sector.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: There is, indeed, growing sentiment on the ground to do away with the "VWO" label.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This conversation brought to fore by NCSS in 2016 should continue.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It is not enough to trim our sails.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I request the Government, our stakeholders and sponsors and members of the public to support us.

sections.label: Objectives of charity amendments
sections.summary: The proposed amendments aim to protect charities and donors and to enhance the Commissioner of Charities' statutory powers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: First, the objectives of the proposed amendments are rather broad-based, that is, (a) to better protect charities and donors by strengthening the governance, accountability and transparency of charities and fundraisers and (b) enhancing the statutory powers of the Commissioner of Charities to maintain public trust and confidence.

sections.label: Disqualifying terrorism-linked persons
sections.summary: The amendments disqualify persons convicted of terrorism, its financing or money laundering from positions of authority in charities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: It is, therefore, timely that we ensure that our charities and fundraising efforts are well run, and with their stakeholders exercising and executing their fiduciary duties as per the rules and regulations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: I welcome the amendments, which have been tweaked to prevent person or persons of dubious standing and with integrity issues from holding key positions or indirectly managing the affairs of another charity-linked entity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: In this respect, and in view of the global security climate, charities and persons associated with them who are convicted of terrorism or of its financing and/or money laundering, will be disqualified from positions of authority.

sections.label: Crowdfunding sites code of practice
sections.summary: The Sunday Times reported on 31 December that crowdfunding sites will be issued a code of practice.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: On 31 December, The Sunday Times reported that crowdfunding sites will be issued with a code of practice, and this the Minister had mentioned earlier.

sections.label: Redefining fundraising appeal
sections.summary: The Bill deletes the listing of the definition of fundraising appeal to the public and replaces it with a new definition.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Under the amendment Bill, the listing of definition of fundraising appeal to members of the public will be deleted and replaced by a new set of definition.

sections.label: Concerns over fundraising scope
sections.summary: The speaker is concerned the new definition may extend fundraising appeal coverage to unsolicited, private, school, association and religious donations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I have some concerns with this change of definition and coverage of fundraising appeal, especially the extent of its scope of coverage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: It appears that the coverage may now extend to unsolicited donations, private donations or fundraising in schools, associations and religious organisations.

sections.label: Ministry on private fundraising
sections.summary: The Ministry said in public consultation comments that fundraising was intended to include private fundraising in schools, associations and religious organisations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The Ministry stated in their comments to public consultation feedback that they intended for fundraising to include private fundraising activities within schools, associations and religious organisations.

sections.label: Online charity and crowdfunding code
sections.summary: Singaporeans raise funds and volunteers online for charity, and a crowdfunding code of practice will be launched this month by the Commissioner of Charities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: There are amazing Singaporeans who raise funds and gather volunteers online to carry out acts of charity and kindness, such as providing meal vouchers, food, daily necessities or supermarket vouchers to elderly folks or households who may be struggling financially.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I read from press reports that a code of practice for crowdfunding platform will be launched this month by the Commissioner of Charities.

sections.label: Fundraising appeal definition concerns
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether the changed fundraising appeal definition burdens charities and non-charity fundraisers, and how the Government weighs foreign versus local causes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Overall, without the benefit of looking at the fine print changes in the fundraising regulations, I am concerned whether the change in the definition of the coverage of fundraising appeal will make it too onerous for charities, especially smaller charities with limited resources or volunteers in these charities, as well as non-charity fundraisers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: How does the Government see that such a ratio will continue to benefit charities or any organisation raising funds for a foreign charitable cause?

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: How does the Government weigh that against the benefit of our locally-based charity helping to raise funds for a worthy foreign charitable cause?

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I am aware that there are exceptions to this rule, but for those who are not excluded from the rule application, is it time to review this requirement or just the current ratio?

sections.label: Crowdfunding code implementation timing
sections.summary: The speaker welcomes the announced Code of Practice on crowdfunding and asks when it will be implemented.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Earlier, Minister had shared there is going to be a Code of Practice on crowdfunding.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I welcome this and also wish to know when this will be implemented.

sections.label: Commissioner action on suspicious campaigns
sections.summary: Citing Gerard Ee on practical difficulties reading every online post, the speaker asks if the Commissioner of Charities has stopped suspicious online campaigns.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The Charity Council chairman, Mr Gerard Ee, very aptly pointed out in a news article in August 2017 that there are "practical difficulties" for the COC to read through every post online to suss out suspicious campaigns, making it difficult to uncover groups that misuse donations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Therefore, I would like to ask the Ministry if there were any past cases where the COC had successfully taken action to stop suspicious online campaigns.

sections.label: Disqualifying fraud and deception convictions
sections.summary: The passage states that no one will dispute the need to disqualify persons convicted of offences involving fraud and deception.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: No one will dispute the need to disqualify persons with convictions for offences involving fraud and deception.

sections.label: Crowdfunding platforms verify recipient information
sections.summary: The soon-to-be-launched code of practice for crowdfunding platforms will require such websites to verify information provided by potential recipients.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The code of practice for crowdfunding platforms, which will be launched soon, will require such websites to verify the information provided by potential recipients.

sections.label: Central databases for charities
sections.summary: The speaker suggests making MSF and CDC central databases available to approved personnel at registered charities so websites can verify information.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: If these websites were to be able to verify the information, the above may not have happened.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: We should consider making the central databases at MSF and Community Development Councils (CDCs) available to approved and qualified personnel at registered charities.

sections.label: More powers for Commissioner
sections.summary: The Commissioner of Charities should get more powers to help run a charity in distress, including when key personnel are suspended, removed or in internal tussles.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Next, to strengthen the governance of our charities and fundraisers, the Commissioner of Charities should be provided with more powers to assist with the running of a charity in distress, particularly when key personnel have been suspended or removed, or when they are in the midst of internal tussles.

sections.label: CDC as IPC, charity numbers
sections.summary: The speaker's CDC is classified as an IPC governed by the Charities Act, and Singapore had almost 2,300 registered charities in 2016.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The CDC of which I am Mayor is also classified as an IPC governed by the Charities Act.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: There are almost 2,300 registered charities in Singapore in 2016.

sections.label: Charity sector annual receipts
sections.summary: The charity sector's overall annual receipt is $16.4 billion, of which $2.7 billion are public donations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The overall annual receipt, that is, Government grants, donations and fees of the charity sector, is $16.4 billion.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Out of this, $2.7 billion are donations by the public.

sections.label: Controversial charity cases
sections.summary: Along with more charities, there have been high profile controversial cases: NKF in 2005, Ren Ci, City Harvest Church and recently the Bone Marrow Donor Programme.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Along with the rise in the number of charities are also high profile controversial cases, starting from the 2005 National Kidney Foundation (NKF) saga, Ren Ci and then the City Harvest Church and, recently, the Bone Marrow Donor Programme.

sections.label: Verifying online fundraising appeals
sections.summary: The speaker asks how the COC plans to verify the authenticity of online fundraising appeals and how donations are disbursed.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: As online fundraising appeals become more common, how does the COC plan to verify the authenticity of the appeals and how donations are disbursed?

sections.label: Protection for charity key persons
sections.summary: Section 46A of the Charities Act protects the Commissioner and officers, but there is no corresponding protection for Key Persons who act in good faith.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Whereas section 46A of the Charities Act protects the Commissioner, his Deputy Commissioner, his Assistant Commissioner or any officers appointed by the Commissioner, or any Sector Administrator, by guaranteeing "no action, suit or other legal proceedings shall be taken" for anything done in good faith.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: There is no corresponding protection for the "Key Persons", some of whom are volunteers, which includes key staff and board members who have acted in good faith.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Bearing in mind that many board members are busy people, volunteers with their own day jobs and many key staff in charities do their best within the constraints of the charities, surely, the Ministry should provide some assurance in the Act that they would be protected from liability if they prove to have acted in good faith and also perhaps consider liability insurance as an industry practice for board members and key officers.

sections.label: Costs of charity governance
sections.summary: Governance costs, audits and multiple funder reports add to operational costs, so the COC is urged to study sector governance costs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: In one of the larger-sized charities that I am involved in, the cost of governance can rise to as high as more than $90,000, and that is not including the pro bono legal services and secretariat services that it obtains from its board members and the time spent to work with the internal and external auditors or professionals.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Each fundraising event also carries the cost of an audit of the financial statements of each event.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: There are also additional hidden costs when charities, for example, run services funded sometimes by more than one funder and then are obliged to produce multiple reports for one same programme as a condition for receiving the grants.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: All these items add to the operational cost of both large and small charities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: I therefore urge the COC to conduct a study of the different sectors under its Administrators to determine if the costs of governance in each of its sector is too low, just nice or too high, and then to provide the necessary support and to rectify the situations as needed.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: In 2015, the group offers yet another angle to measure the effectiveness of governance using a self-assessment thermometer to determine if governance might be too heavy or too light.

sections.label: Charities Amendment Bill update
sections.summary: The Charities (Amendment) Bill is described as a good attempt to update governance regulations to keep up with the times.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The Charities (Amendment) Bill is a good attempt to update the governance regulations to keep up with the times.

sections.label: Revised fundraising appeal definition
sections.summary: The revised definition of fundraising appeal in clause 10 may dampen funding for the charity sector.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: First, the revised definition of "fundraising appeal" as proposed in clause 10 may have a dampening effect on funding for the charity sector.

sections.label: Permits for foreign fundraising
sections.summary: Charities raising funds for foreign purposes must apply for a permit, and this now extends to private events.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Furthermore, charities raising funds for foreign purposes need to apply for a permit, and this requirement now extends to private events.

sections.label: Charity Transparency Awards recipients
sections.summary: Only 41 charities made the cut on disclosure and transparency among those assessed by the Charity Council.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: On support for charities, I refer to the recent Charity Transparency Awards, noting that only 41 out of the possible hundreds or even thousands of charities assessed by the Charity Council made the cut on disclosure and transparency.

sections.label: Support for smaller charities
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Ministry has looked at ways to better support charities, especially smaller ones, beyond those the Minister mentioned.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Has the Ministry looked at ways we can better support charities, other than those that the Minister had mentioned in the Opening speech, especially the smaller ones?

sections.label: Mandatory electronic filing of submissions
sections.summary: The Bill proposes to mandate electronic filing of annual submissions to increase transparency and boost accountability.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: To increase transparency and boost accountability, the Bill proposes to mandate the electronic filing of annual submissions.

sections.label: Separate accounts and fund ratios
sections.summary: The passage suggests requiring charities to keep separate accounts for operations and charities fund accounts, and considering ratios for deposits into the fund account.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: To this end, I would also suggest that we require charities to maintain separate accounts for operations and for the charities fund accounts, similar to practices by law firms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: We can consider setting ratios where a certain percentage of each dollar raised must be deposited into the charities' fund account for the approved and designated use.

sections.label: Registration rules for online fundraisers
sections.summary: The passage suggests considering requiring online fundraisers based here to register in Singapore, keep accounts in Singapore, and have at least two Singaporean directors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: At the very least, for online fundraisers based here, we should consider requiring them to be registered in Singapore and for the accounts to be maintained in Singapore, and at least two of the directors should be Singaporeans.

sections.label: Clarifying definition, not extending scope
sections.summary: The proposed amendments in the Bill serve to clarify the definition, not extend its scope.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: The amendments that we have proposed in this Bill, Mr Deputy Speaker, serve to clarify the definition, not extend its scope.

sections.label: Exempting small-scale fundraising appeals
sections.summary: The Regulations are being revised to keep up with the charity sector, with intent to exempt small-scale and private fundraising appeals from certain requirements.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: We are revising our Regulations to keep up with the needs of the charity sector.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: We intend to exempt small-scale and private fundraising appeals from certain requirements.

sections.label: 80:20 rule remains
sections.summary: The 80:20 rule will remain for now after a review.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: Mr Dennis Tan also asked for my views on this matter.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: We have reviewed this and we felt that at this point in time, the 80:20 rule will remain for now.

sections.label: Code of Practice industry standard
sections.summary: Co-developing a practical and workable Code of Practice aims to set an industry standard of good practices instilling transparency and accountability.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: By co-developing a practical and workable Code of Practice, we aim to set an industry standard of good practices that will instil transparency and accountability in the sector.

sections.label: Code of Practice not mandatory
sections.summary: The Code of Practice will not be mandatory, but the Commissioner will lend weight to promote its adoption.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: While the Code of Practice will not be made mandatory, the Commissioner will lend weight to promote its adoption.

sections.label: Charities with small annual receipts
sections.summary: About 50% of charities in Singapore have annual receipts of less than $250,000.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: About 50% of charities in Singapore have annual receipts of less than $250,000.

sections.label: Cap on fundraising expenses
sections.summary: Charities are currently required to cap fundraising expenses in any given year to not more than 30% of total funds raised.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: On Members' concerns about controls on the use of funds raised, points mentioned by Mr Gan Thiam Poh and Ms Thanaletchimi, charities are currently required to cap their fundraising expenses in any given year to not more than 30% of total funds raised.

sections.label: Suspension period capped at 24 months
sections.summary: The total period of such suspensions, including extensions, are proposed to be capped at 24 months.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: The total period of such suspensions, including any extensions of the suspensions, are proposed to be capped at 24 months.

sections.label: Disqualification of unfit charity persons
sections.summary: The Bill proposes to disqualify persons convicted of terrorism, terrorism financing or money laundering to strengthen the disqualification and removal regimes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: On the disqualification and removal regimes, our objective is to ensure that charities are managed by fit and proper persons who will help maintain public trust and confidence in the sector.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: Hence, to strengthen the regime, the Bill proposes to explicitly provide that persons convicted of terrorism, terrorism financing or money laundering will be disqualified.

sections.label: FATF charity terrorism financing cases
sections.summary: FATF has recorded over 100 cases worldwide of alleged abuse of charities for terrorism financing.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: FATF has recorded over 100 cases worldwide of alleged abuse of charities for terrorism financing.

sections.label: Commissioner reviews charity sector vulnerabilities
sections.summary: The Commissioner has carried out targeted reviews and worked with law enforcement agencies to monitor charity sector vulnerabilities, though no action was taken under the Act.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: While we have not taken action under the Act against charities for money laundering or terrorism financing-related offences, the Commissioner has carried out targeted reviews and worked closely with the law enforcement agencies to monitor the vulnerabilities that the charity sector may be exposed to.

sections.label: 2017 learning event attendance
sections.summary: In 2017, more than 1,600 participants attended learning events.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: In 2017, more than 1,600 participants attended our learning events.

sections.label: Charity funding and electronic filing
sections.summary: Charities can tap the VWOs-Charities Capability Fund, and fewer than 100 of about 2,200 registered charities still file hardcopy submissions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: Charities can also tap on the VWOs-Charities Capability Fund to support their efforts in improving their governance and management capabilities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: On electronic filing, in response to Mr Melvin Yong's question, fewer than 100 of our registered charities are still filing hardcopy submissions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: So, the large majority of the rest of the 2,200 or so charities have already gone on to electronic filing.

sections.label: Sector Administrators assisting Commissioner
sections.summary: The Commissioner is assisted by five Sector Administrators from MOH, MOE and MSF who understand their sectors' needs and essential services.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: The Commissioner is assisted by the five Sector Administrators in various Ministries and agencies − MOH, MOE and MSF − who will best understand the needs of their respective sectors, including which ones are working closely with them, providing essential services that are required to serve the needs of the community.
